summary: The audit checks 45 units of coursework, every course letter graded with a B or better: the NEPR core courses including three quarters of NEPR 280, BIOS 217 and one graduate statistics course of 3 or more units from the list. Checked by hand: six pre-approved units of advanced courses (at least one for 3 units or more), the SIN Boot Camp, the neuroanatomy sessions, the thesis proposal and defense, finishing courses before TGR, and that no course also counts toward a PhD.

program.why: Grading: "All courses used for the Neurosciences M.S. must be taken for a letter grade and passed with a 3.0 (B) or better."

xGC5J2VZ.why: "3 quarters of NEPR 280 (Journal Club) are required." NEPR 280 is repeatable, so it is listed three times. The letter grade and B rule ("All courses used for the Neurosciences M.S. must be taken for a letter grade and passed with a 3.0 (B) or better") is program-wide.

X28z06Gq.why: "Students must complete [BIOS 217] as well as one (1) graduate statistics course from the list below; pre-approval is required." The list reads "Earn at least 3 credits from the following": one course, of 3 or more units.

8kwksqw0.why: "Six units of advanced neuroscience coursework are required. To complete the six units, at least one course must be three units or more ... Pre-approval for advanced courses is required." No list: the student moves the approved courses in.

bZYQ9tbW.why: "The student must defend the thesis project through oral presentation to the Master's thesis committee by the end of the 2nd year."

add.why: "Students must also complete the Stanford Immersive Neurosciences (SIN) Boot Camp."
"Students must complete special sessions in neuroanatomy."
